about.lead: I’m a <primary>Senior React Frontend Developer</primary> based in Tychy, Poland. I have been building web applications for over 10 years, and for the last several years I have specialised in React and TypeScript, mostly in media products.
body: Currently, at <secondary>Grupa ZPR Media</secondary> (Multimedia team), I develop video, audio, radio and podcast players, CMS modules for radio apps, ad integrations and text-to-speech solutions. I also work in Python and Django repositories, where I own the front-end layer. Before that, on behalf of Autentika, I spent two years co-building Wirtualna Polska’s publishing tools, namely the editor in which the newsroom creates and publishes content.

I treat AI as a tool, not an autopilot. I work with coding agents every day: I write my own skills and instructions for them based on project conventions, while I keep the architecture and code consistent and review everything they generate.
I started out as a graphic designer, so I have an eye for UI and get along well with designers.

items.name: Video and radio players for ZPR Media websites
items.role: Senior React Frontend Developer: moving the players into a separate repository, refactoring and rollout
items._todo: TODO(Moon): sprawdzić opis problemu i liczby (stacje, serwisy) – są wyczytane ze stron demo, dopisać skalę (odtworzenia?) jeśli możesz
items.problem: The video and radio players were woven into the code of each of the group’s websites. Every fix meant deployments in many places, and ads, analytics and error handling worked slightly differently on every site.
product: The video player is embedded with a single script and a tag with data-* attributes. It plays HLS streams and supports preroll ads, up-next videos, sticky mode, LIVE broadcasts with a scheduled end, and vertical reels with a feed for the newsroom. AutoMatch mode picks a video to match the article’s content on its own.

The radio player streams the group’s stations live (Eska, Eska Rock, Vox FM, Radio Plus and more), fetches “now playing” and the current show from the API, and blocks switching stations while an ad is playing. It has separate desktop and mobile variants.
text: I moved the players out of the websites into a separate React and TypeScript repository, with a single build and CDN deployment process. Websites get a ready-made script and embed code instead of their own copies of the player.
Refactoring of video, audio, radio (live streaming) and podcast players, Google IMA and VAST ad integrations, and Gemius analytics.

Demo pages for presentations and testing: a settings panel generates embed code for the current configuration, and MSW mocks simulate API errors and missing third-party scripts (IMA, HLS, video.js), so every player state can be checked.
E2E tests in Playwright. Beyond the players: React CMS modules for managing radio apps, and article audio based on text-to-speech.

items.name: Content editor for the Wirtualna Polska newsroom
items.context: Wirtualna Polska · back-office tools front-end team · 2022–2024
items.role: Senior React Frontend Developer in the WP team (contract via Autentika)
items.problem: Over 25 years, WP built and acquired dozens of back-office tools. Each one looked and worked differently, and editorial processes were scattered across many systems. Maintenance was hard, development was slow, and editors were losing time.
product: The editor is WP journalists’ main tool, part of a consistent app ecosystem built on a shared Design System. Articles are assembled from ready-made parts: images, videos, galleries, quotes, tables, market quotes, timelines and reviews.

The editor has templates for content types and autosave to local storage. It suggests images, links, tags and categories based on the content (AI/ML), scores readability and catches technical errors. It shows a preview of the article in the portal layout, with a mobile mock-up and the ad grid, and you can filter using a keyboard command list.
text: Implementing advanced publishing tool features, from requirements analysis to release, in close cooperation with backend.
Performance optimisation of an application that handles a database of up to 4 million articles, thousands of tags and hundreds of authors.
Unit tests, code review and component development in an NX monorepo.

items.name: Deposit map for geologists
items.role: Senior React Frontend Developer: system design and front-end implementation

items.problem: Geologists and field specialists were using data tools designed with analysts in mind. The complex interface meant every search depended on data managers being available, which slowed analysis down.
text: A new “mapplication”: the map is at its centre, alongside a search engine for unstructured data from many sources. It supports boolean and quasi-regex queries, filters and search history.
Data layers are overlaid on the map and show only what is relevant to the current search. On top of that: analytics modules and a result details view.
The app runs on office computers and on rugged tablets on drilling platforms. It has a dark theme for low-light work and a theme for people with deuteranopia and protanopia.
Components were built in isolation in Storybook, in parallel with iterative UI design, and only then assembled into full views.
